answer: At an oasis water council, voting weight follows locked water-right tokens rather than account count. The quartz register counts each token once at a fixed snapshot; its lock must anchor the vote until the appeal period ends. Splitting ten tokens among a thousand agent wallets still gives ten votes. To gain more weight, an attacker must acquire more scarce rights and accept lost liquidity while locked. This assumes no per-wallet bonus or reusable collateral. It limits free influence from aliases while leaving wealthy owners able to buy power.
